A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the climate system is not only very sensitive to changes in atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations, but also very fast to respond to these changes, and that this fast response should not be neglected in any climate change policy.

the CMIP5 models are not yet well calibrated for abrupt CO2 changes, but they are consistent with the expectation that the climate system is a low-pass filter that will not respond to abrupt changes in CO2 concentration on short time scales.

a simple exponential function is a good first-order approximation for the temperature response of the climate system to a CO2 increase but is not a good approximation for the time required to reach a specified amount of warming.
